Fake Law Firm Exposed

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We expose the illusive Tsepiso Harinnyane Hlapi - the man behind a string of scam labour law firms who take on retrenched employees cases, only to never pay them out their settlements

Unique Selling Point:
Imagine you've been unfairly dismissed during the Covid-19 pandemic. You search the web and find what appears to be the perfect law firm to handle your case on https://www.employmentlaw-experts.co.za. Their website looks legit, they promise the world and best of all they take on your case on a "No Win, No Fees" basis. After consulting with you, mostly via Whatsapp, they approach your former employers and get a settlement on your behalf. But the settlement is paid directly to Employment Law Experts accounts, and you never see your money again. That's exactly what's happened to many case studies who have approached Carte Blanche with their stories.

Summary:
Initially, we did not know who was behind the scam. Our case studies did not even know where Employment Law Experts offices were. Monies were paid into another scam law firm's account, SPOMOP PTY LTD. Spomop's website has been suspended, their physical address does not exist, and when pushed for answers they stop taking calls. They still have an active Facebook page. But an insider has spilled the beans, and we now know that the person known to our case studies as T Harry, AKA Michael, AKA Harry is actually Tsepiso Harinnyane Hlapi. Hlapi is not a lawyer, lives in an upmarket house in Dainfern, and has a long history of running the same scam. A CIPC search revealed he is the active director of several other labour law firms: Labourdex, Labour Law Assist, Labourzone etc. None of these have active websites, but a HelloPeter search reveals scores of exactly the same complaints about these firms - they got settlements but never paid out.

Further information:
Suggested Treatment:

We take our presenter through the process of tracking down the firms, visit the supposed offices and addresses only to find nothing, and ask the question who is behind the scam. Then we reveal its Hlapi, show his connections to the other fake firms, show how he has setup Spomop using a director who does not exist, and confront him at his house in Dainfern.

We have good case studies, as well as an actual lawyer who worked for Employment Law Experts for two weeks before quitting because of the irregularities who are willing to speak on camera.

There are also some other nice elements, Employment Law Experts on their website say they will take on your case for 33% of your settlement - in South Africa lawyers can only take 25%. They also advise people not to use the CCMA,(otherwise the scam won't work) but the CCMA is a completely FREE service to the public.

Script:


Fake Law Firm
1st Draft Script
7 October 2020

Voice
Approximately 3 million people have lost their jobs since the start of the national lockdown. Many felt they had been unfairly dismissed, but few could afford the expensive legal fees needed to take on their former employers.

Link Mac
So if you were retrenched during lockdown, and came across a website offering to fight your case with your former employers on a “No Win, No Fees” basis, it might sound like the perfect solution - or not.

Voice
Capetonian Vanishree Govender is one of several viewers from across the country who’ve complained to us about this company - Employment Law Experts. Govender came across them in June this year after she lost her job. By the looks of the impressive website, she thought she was dealing with a law firm.

Sound Up Vanishree Govender
I felt it was an unfair dismissal, so I came across the Emloyment Law Experts.

Voice
It was one of the first sites she found - and they made a no win no fees offer, so Govender contacted them.

Sound Up Vanishree
And I filled in the you know, the call me back details. So what they did was, they forwarded me an email, with some forms to fill, so I filled that in and sent it back to them.

Voice
The documents she signed contained her personal details, information on her former employers and a POA or power of attorney.

Sound Up Vanishree
They send you an email to say that they are going to be contacting you further, within 3 to 10 days or something like that, working days.

Voice
She never heard from them again - but to her shock she soon found out that they’d approached her former employers, reached a settlement on her behalf, and had been paid out for it.

Sound Up Vanishree
Mac: Ok, and how much money was it that your previous employer paid to them?

Vanishree: They got I think around R54 000.

Mac: So that was the settlement that they’d negotiated with your employer?

Vanishree: Without my permission ja. So I didn’t know about any negotiations,

Voice
Employment Law Experts say if they win your case, they keep 33% of the settlement, and pay you the rest. But Govender says months later she has not received anything - not exactly what she was promised on their website.

Sound Up Vanishree
Mac: Did they at any point pay you anything?

Vanishree: No, nothing.

Mac: Nothing?

Vanishree: Nothing. I never heard from them again.

Voice
Tammy Higgins from Johannesburg also took her case to Employment Law Experts, after she struggled to find help during the initial few weeks of South Africa’s hard lockdown.

Sound Up Tammy
They were literally the first company that came up, everything was closed, it was Covid, so I had no means to pay for legal representation. So they worked on a contingency basis.

Voice
Higgins thought Employment Law Experts were going to represent her at the CCMA, but she says that never happened.

Sound Up Tammy
Up to the day before my case at the CCMA, Employment Law Experts hadn’t heard one single fact about my case.

Voice
Fed up with the poor service, she fired them a day before her hearing at the CCMA.

Sound Up Tammy
I actually told them, I terminated my service with them.

Voice
But unbeknown to her, Employment Law Experts were trying to get her former employers to pay out a settlement agreement in the background.

Sound Up Tammy
Tammy: They had gotten in touch with my previous employer, without my knowledge, and requested a settlement.

Mac: So this whole time that they are stringing you along, this whole time that you are interacting with them, they are not saying anything about contacting your company?

Tammy: No

Voice
Although her employers refused to pay them, Higgins lost her case at the CCMA and feels she could have done better with proper legal representation. Despite all appearances, Employment Law Experts is not in fact a law firm. We wanted to put the allegations to them, but to speak to anyone from the company seems to be impossible.


Sound Up Macfarlane calling and Titles saying call 1, call 2 etc

Call 1: 5-5-2, please leave your message after you hear the tone.

Call 2: 1-0, you don’t need to leave a message.

Call 3: 8-2, please leave a message after you hear the tone.

Voice
Having had no joy with any of their known numbers we tried calling their senior legal manager Michael, who - according to their website - was online and available to chat on whatsapp.

Sound Up Macfarlane
This is the answering service for 065….

Sound Up Macfarlane
So we’ve been trying relentlessly to get a hold of these guys but it’s near impossible, so we’re going to pretend to be a client, because they’ve got a whatsapp number on their website, and see how quickly they respond. Maybe find out whats up on their whatsapp? Lets see how this works, right, so “Hi I have lost my job, can you help”. O wow, that was less than two seconds. “Hi welcome to legal advisor, thank you for your enquiry how may we help you.” It’s unbelievable how fast this thing is. I wish they could answer their phones as quickly as this automated system.

Voice
We decided to pay them a visit at their offices in the Nelson Mandela Square in Sandton. The address led us to a communal office space rented to many companies, who all share a central reception area. The receptionist said she’d never actually met anyone from Employment Law Experts.

Sound Up Reception
Receptionist: So they sign up on-line, so it’s not always we get to meet our virtual office clients, so…

Mac: But do they ever come here though?

Receptionist: They’ve never come here.

Mac: Am I the first person to come here looking for them?

Receptionist: No you’re not.

Mac: People are always looking for them?

Receptionist: Ja.

Link Mac
So we’ve just been to the upmarket offices of Employment Law Experts here in Sandton, but even the people here have never seen them. Apparently it’s a virtual office, I wonder what that means?

Voice
So who’s behind the carefully crafted veneer that is Employment Law Experts? Our investigation led us to two names. Employment Law Experts is registered under the name Spomop Pty Ltd, but is trading as Employment Law Experts. Spomop is the same company into which employers pay the settlement amounts. Spomop’s director is a man called Vuwani Magidi. According to sources, another man, known only to employees as Harry T, is in charge of the daily running of the business. This image which was leaked to us, shows some of the aliases Harry used, including his real name, Tsepiso Hlapi.
But not even former employees have met him in person. This woman, who we’ll call Mrs X, is a registered attorney who worked for them for all of two weeks during the lockdown before calling it quits.

Sound Up Mrs X
Mrs X: I only officially started I think on about the 17th of June.

Mac: Ok

Mrs X: I officially resigned on the 2nd of July.

Mac: That’s two weeks. You only lasted two weeks?

Mrs X: I lasted two weeks.

Voice
She says all her interactions were with a man who called himself Harry, whom she only ever spoke to over digital communications like video conferencing app Zoom. Harry told her they were a start up company, and one of her first tasks was to hire the employees whose job it would be to negotiate settlements on behalf of Employment Law Experts.

Sound Up Mrs X
And what was unusual about that, was he wasn’t looking for attorneys or legally trained people, or anyone even trained in industrial relations or human resources. He wanted sales people.

Voice
She raised several concerns about how Employment Law Experts were doing business with Harry, but got no answers. The final straw was complaints she saw about the company.

Sound Up Mrs X
And I asked Harry and I said these complaints are coming in to your Facebook page about that my employer has been swindled out of money, I haven’t been paid the money.

Voice
Having got no satisfactory answers from Harry, she soon quit. But a few days later she got a disturbing call from one of the “sales” people still working for Employment Law Experts.

Sound Up Mrs X
And she said they are using your name when they are emailing clients. And I was like sorry, what? No they are using your name.

Voice
In this emailed response to Mrs X by a person only identifying themselves as Vee, Employment Law Experts claimed her name was used due to the automated nature of the email system and that her details had since been removed. She’s reported the incident to both the Legal Practice Council, Law society and the SAPS. Our complainants believe Employment Law Experts is nothing but an elaborate scam.

Sound Up Vanishree
It is completely a scam, this company does not exist, it’s completely a fraud.



Voice
Tsepiso Hlapi is listed as a director in numerous other companies, which offer the same services. These are some of their online reviews, where members of the public accuse them of outright fraud and theft, all with the same MO as Employment Law Experts.

Sound Up Tammy
I just think its disgusting to be doing this to people who are already in such a tough situation. They are playing with people’s lives.



Voice
Neither Vuwani Magidi nor Tsepiso Hlapi have taken our calls, but in an emailed response from Employment Law Experts, signed only as Management, they said Mr Magidi is currently indisposed and on medical leave, and that they would revert as a matter of urgency. To date they have not answered any of our questions. Meanwhile, Govender and Higgins say they hope that by coming forward they might prevent more people from going through what they did.

Sound Up Vanishree
For many people it is their pay cheque that they are looking for you know, that they need to feed their families.

Sound Up Tammy
They need to stop, and they need to be put in jail. Because its fraud, they are committing fraud, it’s not right.


ENDS







Fake Law Firm Promos

Promo 1
We investigate a company who claim to be experts in employment and labour law litigation, and reveal how they’ve left South Africans retrenched during the national lockdown in dire financial straights.

Promo 2
A fancy website and upmarket offices, but no one’s home. We expose so called law experts that made big promises to retrenched employees, but cost them thousands instead.

Promo 3
No win, no fees - a fantastic offer to those retrenched during the lockdown who wanted to claim from their former employers - only to be left in the lurch by so-called labour law experts.

But an insider has spilled the beans, and we now know that the person known to our case studies as T Harry, AKA Michael, AKA Harry is actually Tsepiso Harinnyane Hlapi. Hlapi is not a lawyer, lives in an upmarket house in Dainfern, and has a long history of running the same scam. A CIPC search revealed he is the active director of several other labour law firms: Labourdex, Labour Law Assist, Labourzone etc. None of these have active websites, but a HelloPeter search reveals scores of exactly the same complaints about these firms - they got settlements but never paid out.
metadata.Further information: Suggested Treatment: We take our presenter through the process of tracking down the firms, visit the supposed offices and addresses only to find nothing, and ask the question who is behind the scam. Then we reveal its Hlapi, show his connections to the other fake firms, show how he has setup Spomop using a director who does not exist, and confront him at his house in Dainfern. We have good case studies, as well as an actual lawyer who worked for Employment Law Experts for two weeks before quitting because of the irregularities who are willing to speak on camera. There are also some other nice elements, Employment Law Experts on their website say they will take on your case for 33% of your settlement - in South Africa lawyers can only take 25%. They also advise people not to use the CCMA,(otherwise the scam won't work) but the CCMA is a completely FREE service to the public.
